questions.problem:
Consider the following system of differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t),$ where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and $u(t)$ is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for ${x}_{p}(t)$ is given below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t)$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{p}^{′}(t)=Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)$

$\text{L6}:\,$ ${u}^{′}(t)={Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that {{field-1}} matrix.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from lines {{field-2}} by substitution.

$\,$ Line $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L7}$ into {{field-3}} .
questions.worked_solution:
Let's examine each statement in turn.

- We first consider line $\text{L4}.$ Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ i.e., by substituting any column $c(t)$ of $Φ$ into the homogeneous system, we get

$$
{c}^{′}(t)=Ac(t),
$$

where ${c}^{′}(t)$ is the corresponding column of derivatives in $Φ.$ As a result, this means that ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ.$ Therefore, $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that $Φ\text{ is a fundamental}$ matrix.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L3}$, $\text{L4},$ and $\text{L5}.$ Let's substitute ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$ from $\text{L4}$ into $\text{L3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)+\cancel{AΦu(t)}=\cancel{AΦu(t)}+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L5}$ follows from $\text{L3}\text{ and }\text{L4}$ by substitution.

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L1},$ $\text{L7},$ and $\text{L8}.$ Substituting

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

from $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φu(t) \\  & =Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L7}$ into  $\text{L1}.$

questions.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}6t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form
$x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+\,\,\frac{1}{4}$ $36t-42$ .
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-t} \\ 3{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}6t \\ 3t\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2{e}^{-2t}\cdot {e}^{-t}-{e}^{-t}\cdot 3{e}^{-2t}}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ -3{e}^{-2t} & 2{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ -3{e}^{-2t} & 2{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -{e}^{2t} \\ -3{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =-[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -{e}^{2t} \\ -3{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3t{e}^{2t} \\ 12t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}-3t{e}^{2t} \\ 12t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int -3t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int 12t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=-3t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=-3\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -3t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t & =(-3t)\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}-\int \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}\cdot (-3\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}t{e}^{2t}+\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}t{e}^{2t}+\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2t} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2t}(1-2t).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=12t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=12\,\text{d}t$ and $v={e}^{t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 12t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t & =12t\cdot {e}^{t}-\int 12\cdot {e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =12t{e}^{t}-12{e}^{t} \\  & =12{e}^{t}(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-t} \\ 3{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2t}(1-2t) \\ 12{e}^{t}(t-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}6(1-2t)+48(t-1) \\ 9(1-2t)+48(t-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}36t-42 \\ 30t-39\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}5t \\ t\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form
$x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}+\,\,\frac{1}{9}$ {{field-1}} .
$-3t-1$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & {e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}5t \\ t\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-t}\cdot {e}^{3t}-{e}^{3t}\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4t{e}^{t} \\ t{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}4t{e}^{t} \\ t{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 4t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int t{e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=4t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=4\,\text{d}t$ and $v={e}^{t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t & =(4t)\cdot {e}^{t}-\int {e}^{t}\cdot (4\,\text{d}t) \\  & =4t{e}^{t}-4{e}^{t} \\  & =4{e}^{t}(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=\,\text{d}t$ and $v=-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t{e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t & =t\cdot (-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t})-\int (-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t})\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{t}{3}{e}^{-3t}+\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{t}{3}{e}^{-3t}-\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t} \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t}(3t+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$

$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form
$x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+\,\,\frac{1}{9}$ {{field-1}} .

questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{t} \\ {e}^{-3t} & 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-3t}\cdot 3{e}^{t}-{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{-3t}}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} \\ -{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2{e}^{-2t}}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} \\ -{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]. \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4t{e}^{3t} \\ -t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}4t{e}^{3t} \\ -t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 4t{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=4t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=4\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4t{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t & =4t\cdot \frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}-\int \frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}\cdot (4\,\text{d}t) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}t{e}^{3t}-\frac{4}{3}\int {e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{4}{3}t{e}^{3t}-\frac{4}{9}{e}^{3t} \\  & =\frac{4}{9}{e}^{3t}(3t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=-t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=-\,\text{d}t$ and $v=-{e}^{-t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t & =(-t)\cdot (-{e}^{-t})-\int (-{e}^{-t})\cdot (-\,\text{d}t) \\  & =t{e}^{-t}-\int {e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =t{e}^{-t}+{e}^{-t} \\  & ={e}^{-t}(t+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{t} \\ {e}^{-3t} & 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{9}{e}^{3t}(3t-1) \\ {e}^{-t}(t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}4(3t-1)+9(t+1) \\ 4(3t-1)+27(t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}21t+5 \\ 39t+23\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3t} & 5{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{-3t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2t\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-3t}\cdot {e}^{t}-5{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{-3t}}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & -5{e}^{t} \\ -{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{4{e}^{-2t}}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & -5{e}^{t} \\ -{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & -5{e}^{3t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =-\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & -5{e}^{3t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}t{e}^{3t} \\ -\frac{1}{2}t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}t{e}^{3t} \\ -\frac{1}{2}t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5}{2}t{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -\frac{1}{2}t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=\frac{5}{2}t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=\frac{5}{2}\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5}{2}t{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t & =(\frac{5}{2}t)\cdot \frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}-\int \frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}\cdot (\frac{5}{2}\,\text{d}t) \\  & =\frac{5}{6}t{e}^{3t}-\frac{5}{6}\int {e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{5}{6}t{e}^{3t}-\frac{5}{18}{e}^{3t} \\  & =\frac{5}{18}{e}^{3t}(3t-1).\end{aligned}

$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3t} & 5{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{-3t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{18}{e}^{3t}(3t-1) \\ \frac{1}{2}{e}^{-t}(t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{18}[\begin{aligned}5(3t-1)+45(t+1) \\ 5(3t-1)+9(t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}30t+20 \\ 12t+2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
